questions.q: How does event-driven integration differ from the Apex HTTP callout integration covered in the Salesforce Integration Development course?
options: Event-driven integration always uses SOAP instead of REST
A callout is synchronous and Salesforce-initiated; event-driven integration announces a fact and lets subscribers react without Salesforce waiting for a response
Event-driven integration can only be used for inbound data, never outbound
There is no real difference; they are the same mechanism with different names
questions.explain: A callout is Salesforce reaching out and waiting for a direct answer. Event-driven integration publishes a fact and moves on, with subscribers reacting independently and asynchronously.

questions.q: Which of these is a correct description of Salesforce's Event Relay feature?
options: It converts a platform event into a custom object record automatically
It is a managed connector that forwards platform/CDC events to Amazon EventBridge without you building a custom subscriber client
It is required before any LWC can use lightning/empApi
It only works with the legacy PushTopic event type
questions.explain: Event Relay is Salesforce's managed, declarative connector to Amazon EventBridge — it forwards platform and CDC events (and can receive events back via EventBridge API destinations) without a hand-built subscriber client.

questions.q: In the order-to-fulfillment example, why does the Apex trigger publish a new custom `Fulfillment_Requested__e` event instead of having the external fulfillment system subscribe directly to the CDC channel on `Order__c`?
options: CDC events cannot be subscribed to by external systems under any circumstances
The custom event lets you expose only the specific fields the fulfillment system needs and fire only on the specific business condition that matters, rather than every raw field change on the object
Custom platform events are always faster to deliver than CDC events
Pub/Sub API cannot subscribe to CDC channels
questions.explain: Chaining CDC into a purpose-built custom event lets the design filter down to the exact condition and payload shape the downstream subscriber actually needs, rather than exposing every raw field change.

questions.q: What does an external system publishing a platform event into Salesforce (rather than Salesforce calling out) let that system do?
options: Bypass all Salesforce security and sharing rules
Notify Salesforce of something happening without Salesforce ever polling or calling out to ask
Directly edit Apex trigger code from outside the org
Avoid using the REST, SOAP, or Pub/Sub APIs entirely
questions.explain: An external publisher can push a platform event into Salesforce via REST, SOAP, or Pub/Sub API, letting an Apex trigger or Flow react — without Salesforce needing to poll or call out to learn about the change.

questions.q: What is one real cost of choosing event-driven integration over a synchronous callout?
options: You lose the immediate, synchronous confirmation a callout gives you, and must account for duplicate delivery and limited ordering guarantees
Event-driven integration cannot be used with Apex at all
Event-driven integration requires disabling all REST APIs in the org
Platform events cannot carry any custom fields
questions.explain: Event-driven integration trades away immediate synchronous confirmation and takes on at-least-once delivery and limited ordering guarantees, in exchange for decoupling the publisher from subscriber availability.
